name: Plant and animal identification
intro: Where the identifier is accurate and consistent, and where one bug gets three answers and a paywall drops after the first scan.

apps.title: Merlin Bird ID by Cornell Lab
apps.short: Merlin Bird ID by Cornell Lab
apps.verdict: From the Cornell Lab, and its core job is identifying birds by sound on a walk, which genuinely pulls people into birdwatching and gets them outside more. But recent updates slipped: sound ID now misses even loud birds, the switch from auto to manual saving annoys people, and the mandatory email registration and buggy login ruin the moment when a bird is about to fly off.
apps.loved: Identifying birds by sound, drawing people into birdwatching, ease of use, being free, history of identified birds
apps.weak: Degraded sound ID after updates, manual saving instead of auto, mandatory email registration, login glitches and occasional crashes
apps.whoFor: Nature lovers and beginning birdwatchers who want to recognize birds by their song on a walk without paying

quotes.text: The app can no longer consistently pick up or identify birds that are calling loudly nearby, even with minimal background noise. Very hit or miss. By contrast, last summer it was able to identify two barred owls deep in the woods.
By the time you get all of the mandatory "name this location" BS and finally hit save the other birds you want to identify will already have left.

apps.title: PlantNet
apps.verdict: People value it for accuracy and being free, using it for years on walks and in the garden to tell flowers from weeds before anything blooms. It breaks on two fronts: US users started getting hit with IP-based blocks, and it only identifies the species, it does not tell you how to care for the plant. Anyone expecting watering and feeding advice will find nothing here.
apps.loved: Identification accuracy, works from leaves and flowers, regional search, geotagging, free to use
apps.weak: IP blocking for US users, no plant care guidance, interface gets more complex with updates, controls disappear when identifying a second plant
apps.whoFor: Gardeners and nature lovers who need an accurate species ID, not a care plan

quotes.text: Easy to use with photos for cross reference & geotagging. I like that I can search by region or worldwide & can narrow search by things like fruits, leaves, flowers etc.

apps.title: iBird Photo Sleuth
apps.verdict: Here recognition genuinely works: people use it as a second opinion to confirm their own guess, and it often lands even on poor or distant shots, pointing toward the right answer when it errs. Complaints are not about accuracy but money and confusion: paying twice, buying a separate app on top of iBird Pro, and the feature vanishing after a reinstall. Some compare it unfavorably to Merlin.
apps.loved: Accurate ID even on poor and distant shots, works as a second opinion to confirm, lots of reference info, constantly updated database, useful for novices
apps.weak: Have to buy it twice and as a separate app on top of iBird Pro, feature vanished after reinstall, Merlin sometimes more accurate, broken feedback contact
apps.whoFor: Bird photographers and growing birders who need to confirm an ID from their own photo

quotes.text: I am not an experienced birder and I have found this app very useful in making bird IDs where the bird is not one that I recognize.
iBird Photo Sleuth will usually help resolve doubt to my identification photo query. Finally, identifying poor quality photos is a great help.
One of my hobbies is wildlife photography, particularly bird photography. So I generally have a photo of the birds I want to identify... I have found this app very useful.

apps.title: Picture Insect: Bug Identifier
apps.verdict: People identify beetles, butterflies, and bites right in the field, keep a personal catalog of found insects, and return to the app again and again. Identification is more often right, but experienced entomologists catch errors around half the time even on local species, you cannot fix a wrong ID, and getting in runs into a paid trial and constant upgrade pop-ups that let the bug get away.
apps.loved: Identifying beetles, butterflies, and bites in the field, a personal insect catalog, info on danger to people and pets, frequently correct identification
apps.weak: Errors around half the time for experienced entomologists, cannot correct a wrong identification, different names for the same insect, paid trial and pushy upgrade pop-ups
apps.whoFor: Nature lovers and gardeners who want to identify insects and bites on the spot and keep a catalog of their finds

quotes.text: I use this app every time I find a bug. Only issue I have with it is it asks to pay for the premium version every time I open the app so sometimes bugs get away.

it's impossible to correct an incorrect ID. The app identified colaspis viridiceps as colaspis brunnea. When I try to correct the ID, it's clear that colaspis viridiceps isn't even in the app, despite it being a common beetle in the southwest U.S.

apps.title: Audubon Bird Guide
apps.verdict: A respected old guide loved for its offline content, maps, sounds, and many photos, used for years to watch birds. It breaks offline: the downloaded field guide stops loading without internet, the very thing people downloaded it for. People are also annoyed by the new account requirement and the lack of bird identification by sound.
apps.loved: Offline content, maps and sounds, many species photos, sighting log, responsive developers
apps.weak: Offline guide fails to load without a connection, new account requirement, no ID by bird sound, search glitches after updates
apps.whoFor: Birdwatchers who want a reference with an offline mode and a log, not sound-based recognition

apps.title: Picture Bird: Bird identifier
apps.verdict: People identify birds by photo and song, and some learn to recognize birds in real life from it, while others use it in wildlife rehab. But sound ID visibly jumps around, the same bird gets three different names, photo ID is wrong for many, and the comparison with Cornell's free Merlin is unflattering, plus the paid subscription is hidden behind a tiny cross.
apps.loved: Identifying birds by photo and song, ease of use, usefulness in wildlife rehab, learning to recognize birds in real life
apps.weak: Unstable sound ID, different names for the same bird, photo-ID errors, subscription hidden behind a tiny cross, losing out to free Merlin
apps.whoFor: Beginning bird lovers who want to identify birds by photo and sound, if a paid trial does not bother them

quotes.text: I've recorded the same bird three times and it's come up with cardinal, hummingbird and owl. It might be a cardinal but there's no way in heck it's the other two.

The Merlin ID app by Cornell university is free. I downloaded this one because it advertised identify bird by feathers, when in fact the app lacks this capacity. No thanks! I'll stick with the free one that's better.
I'd love the app a lot more, but your logo is on WAY TOO LONG when I first open the app. By the time it goes away and I can snap a photo or record a song, the bird has flown away.

apps.title: Picture Mushroom: Identifier
apps.verdict: Many consider Picture Mushroom the best fungi identifier, use it for years, and praise the quality of the AI and the learning content. Two sore spots repeat: they removed the edible-versus-poisonous label and replaced it with a generic warning, pushing some people away, and the same mushroom photographed three times gives three different answers. The 30-a-year price for rare use and the inaccurate location tagging also annoy.
apps.loved: Accurate mushroom identification and good AI, learning content and species cards, a collection of finds, a habit of years
apps.weak: Removed the edibility label, gives different answers on repeat photos of the same mushroom, pricey for occasional use, inaccurate location tagging
apps.whoFor: Foragers and fungi lovers who want a reliable identifier as a first step, with mandatory edibility double-checking

quotes.text: I just bought these from a local fruit and vegetable grocery store. Your app is saying they're toxic. It's calling them white dome caps. And they are snow/seafood mushrooms.

apps.title: Birda - Bird Watching, Birding
apps.verdict: Birda is loved as a social network for birders: a photo feed, comments, badges, challenges, and list-keeping, great for people who want to share rather than just tick boxes. Its one clear weak spot is that the AI photo identification works poorly, so people leave to double-check in Google or Merlin. It can also be sluggish and requires location to be on.
apps.loved: Social feed with photos and comments, badges and challenges, sighting lists, eBird import, identification by both photo and sound planned
apps.weak: Weak AI photo identification, lag and freezing, requires location to be on, no sound identification yet
apps.whoFor: Birders who value community, photo sharing, and list-keeping over accurate auto-identification

apps.title: Birdbuddy: ID & Collect Birds
apps.verdict: This is a smart camera feeder, and it genuinely brings people joy watching birds, filming videos, collecting a bird gallery, and sharing with family. But after updates the automatic bird ID, the very reason people bought the 200-plus-dollar device, was locked behind a subscription, access for a second family member also costs extra, and the flood of dozens of identical sparrow notifications cannot be properly muted.
apps.loved: The joy of watching birds, videos and bird collection, sharing with family, camera photo quality
apps.weak: Automatic bird ID moved behind a subscription after buying the hardware, paid access for a second family member, flood of identical notifications, weak identification accuracy
apps.whoFor: People who want a live camera feeder for the pleasure of watching birds and are willing to pay extra by subscription for identification

apps.title: Identify Birds – Smart Bird ID
apps.verdict: Smart Bird ID appeals to beginner birdwatchers: simple photo and sound identification, a sticker collection, the joy of learning morning birds. Two recurring failures. The app crashes constantly on everything: video, sound, photo upload, changing location. And the ads are aggressive, including a horrifying case where a child was shown a clip of bloody victims. On sound accuracy many honestly rank it below the free Merlin by Cornell.
apps.loved: Simple photo and sound identification, a bird sticker collection, works on weak internet, a handy well-organized database
apps.weak: Frequent crashes on video, sound, photo upload and location change, aggressive and sometimes shocking ads, sound identification worse than the free Merlin
apps.whoFor: Beginner bird lovers who value gamification and simplicity and for whom sound accuracy isn't critical

quotes.text: This is a great app! However, when trying to identify a bird using sound, it doesn't pick up anything! So Merlin's kinda better in that situation.

apps.title: PictureThis - Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: People come to sort out plants in the garden and on the windowsill, and some genuinely gain confidence: they save roses, houseplants, learn which plants are poisonous. But accuracy hovers around 80 percent, experienced gardeners catch it making mistakes and switch to Google's camera, and getting in runs into a subscription and an aggressive self-ad on startup.
apps.loved: Care for roses and houseplants, watering schedule, warnings about poisonous plants, help for garden beginners
apps.weak: Accuracy around 80 percent, mistakes on familiar plants, cannot upload an existing photo, heavy ads on startup, disputed subscription after a short trial
apps.whoFor: Beginning gardeners and houseplant lovers who need a care plan rather than museum-grade identification

quotes.text: I was looking for an app to which you can import a photo you already took to get the id. A friend recommended PictureThis, but alas... You have to use the app to take the picture.

apps.title: Seek by iNaturalist
apps.verdict: People love Seek by iNaturalist for the gamification: it feels like real-life Pokemon, you collect finds and read solid species facts backed by National Geographic. One pain repeats across many reviews: after an update roughly in the past year accuracy dropped sharply, the camera now blurs at close range, and plants often get identified only down to dicots. Being free with no ads keeps loyalty high.
apps.loved: Free with no ads, the thrill of collecting and learning, quality species facts, works on weak internet
apps.weak: Accuracy dropped after an update in the past year, camera blurs up close and won't zoom, plants only identified to family level, no species search
apps.whoFor: Curious naturalists and families who want to learn and collect species for free without needing expert-level precision

quotes.text: No matter what plant I take a picture of 95% of the time it labels it as dicots. Do not recommend this app

apps.title: PlantSnap - Plant Scanner
apps.verdict: People want to quickly learn a flower, tree, or weed from a photo, and for some it works great, they fill their home with plants and learn to care for them. But accuracy is unstable, many cannot get the right name even in three tries, the new version turned clunky, and the developers push ads, upgrades, and spam emails whose unsubscribe button does not work.
apps.loved: Fast identification of flowers, trees, and weeds, detailed plant info, help for beginners, watering journal
apps.weak: Unstable accuracy, wrong names even after several tries, clunky new version, pushy ads and spam emails
apps.whoFor: Curious beginner gardeners who need to quickly identify a plant from a photo and do not require perfect accuracy

quotes.text: One of the features I see fascinating is its fast and easy to explore you can journal days you water your plant and days you missed

apps.title: Bird Song Id USA songs & calls
apps.short: Bird Song Id USA songs & calls
apps.verdict: The real strength here is not mic recognition but the library of clear pre-recorded songs and lovely bird photos people use to learn calls. One user who lost their sight reconnected with the outdoors through the sounds. Live recording, though, is fussy: sensitive to background noise, often says the mic is unavailable on newer iPhones, and the app has not been updated in a long time.
apps.loved: Clear pre-recorded songs and calls, beautiful bird photos, learning birds by ear, helps the visually impaired
apps.weak: Fussy mic recording, errors on background noise, mic unavailable on newer iPhones, dated interface, no recent updates
apps.whoFor: Beginners and hobbyists learning bird calls from samples, not those trying to capture recordings in the field

quotes.text: Since upgrading to iPhone 14, when trying to record bird calls, a message says not able to record with this device.

apps.title: Free Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: Free Plant Identifier gets praise for simplicity, a large plant database, and a convenient results screen with diagnostics. The main catch is the name itself: only a couple of IDs a day are free, disease diagnosis and the rest sit behind payment, and there's a lot of ads in between that heat up the phone. Accuracy is middling, and the same photo on different days gives different answers.
apps.loved: Simplicity and a large plant database, convenient info and diagnostics, spotting weeds and invasive species
apps.weak: Free means only a couple of IDs a day, diagnosis and the essentials cost money, heavy ads, the phone heats up, inconsistent accuracy
apps.whoFor: Undemanding users needing one-off IDs who can tolerate ads and the free-tier limits

apps.title: iplant - Plant Identification
apps.verdict: A free crowd-sourced identifier with no subscription, which people love and use in school classes, and the consistency of its result earns trust unlike its rivals. But you pay with attention: ads on open, before submitting a photo, layered over another ad, and because of them the shot gets lost and you have to retake it several times. Accuracy is middling, it sometimes returns just tree instead of a maple species, and descriptions occasionally come in Chinese rather than English.
apps.loved: Free and no subscription, a stable repeatable result earns trust, handy in class, simple ID from a photo
apps.weak: A flood of ads on every action, the photo gets lost to ads and needs retaking, descriptions sometimes in Chinese, results too generic like just tree
apps.whoFor: Students and anyone wanting free plant ID who can tolerate ads in exchange for no subscription

quotes.text: Tried several apps and they gave me a different ID on one plant every time I submitted a photo. This app comes up with the same result every time so I trust the results more.
I expected a bit more info on tree I'd than "maple" Absolutely worthless. I took a picture of a maple tree sapling 6" high. The iplant I'd?: Tree

apps.title: Bird Identifier: BirdScope
apps.verdict: People praise it for dual identification, by photo and by sound, and for picking a bird's call out of background noise. It breaks on geography and accuracy: it suggests species not from your region, down to a parrot and a bald eagle where they do not exist, and the camera zoom cannot reach a bird at the feeder. Plus a murky auto-renewing subscription after the week-long trial.
apps.loved: Identification by both photo and sound, picks a bird's call out of noise, handy for verifying your own sightings
apps.weak: Suggests birds not from your region, weak camera zoom cannot reach a distant bird, hard to cancel the subscription, auto-renewal after the trial
apps.whoFor: Beginner birders who value sound identification and are not strict about regional accuracy

quotes.text: According to this app we have bald eagles, Japanese grosbeaks and eastern meadowlarks in the central western coast of Mexico. LOL. We definitely do not.

apps.title: PlantIn: Plant Identifier・Care
apps.verdict: The real job here is less about naming the plant and more about suggesting a care routine, and when the advice is right people really do save their plants: they stop overwatering, revive wilting ones. But the app regularly confuses species, gives dubious watering and fertilizing schedules, and its photo-based disease help failed for many, with plants dying anyway.
apps.loved: Watering and care tips, rescuing overwatered plants, poison information, the feeling of having someone to talk plants with
apps.weak: Confuses species with each other, wrong watering and fertilizing schedules, weak disease diagnosis, ads even in the paid version
apps.whoFor: Houseplant owners who care more about reminders and a care routine than precise species identification

apps.title: Plantify: AI Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: The app helps not just name a plant but point out what is wrong and how to treat it, which the people who saved their plants praise. But the diagnosis often fails: for a sweet pea photo it showed succulents with no advice, and for some it names no plant at all. A separate pain is that there is no account tab to cancel, the contact button throws a 404, and after paying for a year people get locked out.
apps.loved: Flags the plant's problem and how to treat it, helped save a money tree, help with gardening
apps.weak: Diagnosis often does not work, confuses plants with succulents, no account tab to cancel, support button throws a 404, locks you out after paying
apps.whoFor: Gardeners who want both ID and plant-care advice and can live with misfires

apps.title: Plant Identifier & Care App
apps.verdict: When it lands, it genuinely helps: it diagnoses overwatering, gives a care schedule, and offers advice for a sick garden plant. But it does not always land, it called a dying snake plant healthy and stumbles on lilac fungus and grass. What angers people most is that the store lists it as free, yet you cannot even scan a plant without paying.
apps.loved: Overwatering diagnosis, care schedules, treatment advice for sick plants, identifies most plants
apps.weak: Listed as free but requires payment to scan, misses on diseases and grass, poorly translated text, calls a dying plant healthy
apps.whoFor: Beginner plant owners who want both identification and care tips and are willing to pay

quotes.text: Saved my favorite plant, It correctly diagnosed an overwatering issue and gave a solid care schedule.

apps.title: Plant Identifier: LeafSnap
apps.verdict: The app is genuinely handy and identifies plants fast, and it saved some people from pulling out a good plant by mistake. But the tech lets it down: sync does not carry over to a new phone, it drains the battery in the field, and it cannot be stopped. The subscription angers people most, the trial charges immediately and the store price does not match the in-app price.
apps.loved: Fast plant identification, detailed care information, simplicity, saves you from weeding out good plants
apps.weak: Data does not transfer to a new phone, sync drains battery and cannot be stopped, charges money instead of a trial, constant subscription nagging
apps.whoFor: Gardeners who want fast identification with care info and can tolerate pushy subscription prompts

apps.title: PlantSnap Pro: Identify Plants
apps.verdict: A one-time purchase instead of a subscription draws people in, and in the desert or for experienced foresters the app sometimes helps for years. But accuracy is around half for many, familiar and common plants get misidentified, the tropics and Caribbean are barely covered, and the old version before the switch to bubbles was clearly better liked than the current one.
apps.loved: One-time payment without a subscription, usefulness in desert climates, identifying both flowers and trees, years of service for some users
apps.weak: Accuracy around half, errors on common plants, weak coverage of the tropics and Caribbean, decline after the version change
apps.whoFor: People who do not want a subscription and can tolerate shaky accuracy as a hint for further checking

apps.title: Plantum - AI Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: This used to be NatureID, where basic identification worked for free and long-time users loved it. Now any photo hits a mandatory payment screen with no way to exit, many call the identification accuracy low, and the paid help from plant experts never actually arrives.
apps.loved: Reliability for some longtime users, the plant-care database, usage history from the old days
apps.weak: Cannot identify a plant without paying, mandatory subscription screen with no exit, low accuracy per many reviews, promised experts do not respond
apps.whoFor: People willing to pay upfront and tolerate shaky accuracy for the care database, not free identification

apps.title: Greg: Plant Identifier & Care
apps.verdict: Greg rides on a friendly tone and community: some people use it for over a year and say their plants survived for the first time thanks to the reminders. There are two weak spots. Many call the watering schedule random and unreliable, ignoring plant size and the fact that the soil is still wet. And the app is buggy: it freezes while typing, won't log in, loses added plants, and misidentifies simple plants like Texas sage.
apps.loved: Friendly tone and community, watering and feeding reminders, clean simple look, helps keep plants alive
apps.weak: Unreliable watering schedule that ignores plant size, freezes and loses added plants, weak plant identification, key features behind a subscription
apps.whoFor: Beginner houseplant owners who value reminders and a warm community, if they can survive the bugs

quotes.text: I wish it was possible to correct known misidentification.
Cute app for tracking and identifying your plants, but the watering schedule is totally unreliable and random.
Watering recommendations should be based on size of the plant, not just size of the pot.

apps.title: Plant Identifier, Care: Planty
apps.verdict: People pick Planty for the plant journal and watering reminders, and that part actually works. Everything else breaks: identification confuses similar cacti and flags diseases on healthy plants, and support ignores emails while still charging 39.99 a month after cancellation. Basic care is there, trust is not.
apps.loved: Plant journal and health tracking, watering and fertilizing reminders, easy start for beginners
apps.weak: Confuses similar plants and gives false diagnoses, the water-all button fails to register, support goes silent, charges continue after cancellation
apps.whoFor: Beginners who want a simple plant diary with reminders and can tolerate shaky identification

quotes.text: Yesterday I clicked "water all" from the checklist. Today I get notifications that my plants are sad and I'm one day late watering... I had to click them all individually.

apps.title: Bird Sounds Identifier Call ID
apps.verdict: People get it to find out who is singing outside on a walk, and it genuinely pulls kids into birdwatching. But it often IDs wrong, offers birds from Asia and Hawaii to someone in Pennsylvania because you cannot set your location, and recordings do not save without a connection. On top of that it pushes the paid subscription hard and is nearly useless without it.
apps.loved: Pulls kids into birdwatching, keeping a list of birds you spot, learning about beautiful birds on a walk
apps.weak: Frequent wrong IDs, no way to set your location, shows birds from the wrong region, recordings do not save offline, pushy subscription prompts, cannot share a recording with friends
apps.whoFor: Parents with kids and beginners who want an excuse to walk and watch birds, not a precise identifier

quotes.text: Often, the birds that I record are described as being found in south Asian or Hawaii and I live in Pennsylvania. Very disappointing.

apps.title: Plant Identifier & Care: Ficus
apps.verdict: Some people were genuinely helped, one saved their anthurium and uses it daily for reminders. But the real complaints outweigh that: it misidentifies tomatoes and trees, one user got poison ivy after trusting the ID, and canceling the subscription is nearly impossible to find. Accuracy hovers around 60 percent.
apps.loved: Watering reminders, helped save houseplants, fast answers, easy to build a plant collection
apps.weak: Wrong plant and disease identification, hidden subscription cancellation, pushy payment prompts, too many tutorial screens
apps.whoFor: Houseplant owners willing to tolerate misses for the sake of care reminders

quotes.text: I remembered the "leaves of 3 let it be" so I downloaded this app to verify before I started ripping some unwanted plants out of my yard. The app said they were ash and box elder. I got poison ivy anyway. Don't rely on it!

apps.title: PlantAI: Identifier & Diagnose
apps.verdict: With a pleasant design and an AI chat for quick questions, the app helps beginners and older gardeners get to grips with plants and keep a log of their plot. But it identifies wrong more than half the time, especially wildflowers, and the promised disease diagnosis gives no more than a free Google or Siri search. Billing gets in the way too: charged on the day of trial cancellation, and after cancelling the yearly plan access is cut for months already paid.
apps.loved: Pleasant design and easy navigation, AI chat for quick questions, keeping a log of plants on the plot, help for beginners and the elderly
apps.weak: Wrong more than half the time, especially on wildflowers, diagnosis no deeper than a free search, charged on the day of trial cancellation, access cut after cancelling
apps.whoFor: Beginners and older gardeners who value a convenient log and general reference over ID accuracy

quotes.text: I know what my plants are, I need to know what problems exist and what can be done. I do not need a photographic album of them. H E L P me save my plants.

apps.title: Bird Identifier, Bird Id
apps.verdict: It names a bird from a photo, and when it lands people praise the quick result plus notes on habitat and feeding. But misses are frequent: it tags every shot as a robin, mistakes a paper bird for a real one, and reads the same photo differently on retries. On top of that, ads flood in after every snap and account activation breaks because the confirmation email never arrives.
apps.loved: Fast recognition on a good shot, habitat and feeding notes, free to start
apps.weak: Frequent misidentifications, same photo read differently, ads after every snap, activation email never arrives, fake scary pop-up about a hacked device
apps.whoFor: Backyard-feeder bird lovers who want a quick hint and do not need pinpoint accuracy

apps.title: AI Plant Identifier - Plant ID
apps.verdict: At first it IDs plants well for many, one user in Costa Rica hit 19 of 20, others enjoy learning that backyard weeds are actually edible. But quality slides over time: the same app starts confusing badly months later, calls every photo out of focus, and stops seeing plants at all. On top sits charging without consent and no way to cancel.
apps.loved: Accurate plant ID early on, fun facts about edible weeds, simple interface, useful for new gardeners
apps.weak: Quality degrades over time, calls every photo out of focus, names the same plant differently each time, 39.99 charged without consent, impossible to cancel
apps.whoFor: Beginner gardeners wanting a quick intro to plants, willing to risk the billing

apps.title: Plant App: Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: The job is the same, learn the plant and what is wrong with it, but the app handles it poorly: for many, identification simply returns nothing, three photos of one tree give three different names, and wrong care advice is dangerous for real plants. On top of that, recovering the account after every major update loses all saved plants.
apps.loved: Simplicity for beginners, occasionally correct identification, cases where it helped spot a plant problem
apps.weak: Identification often returns nothing, different names for the same plant, dangerously wrong care advice, loss of saved plants after updates
apps.whoFor: Maybe only outright beginners with no accuracy demands, but per the reviews almost everyone should look for an alternative

quotes.text: I took three pictures of the same tree and it gave me three different names. This app is garbage.

apps.title: LensAI・Identifier・Image Search
apps.verdict: The idea appeals, one identifier for plants, animals, insects and dog breed in one place, and some value that it replaces a stack of separate apps. But accuracy lets it down: it confuses a moth with a beetle, a basset with a dachshund, and on snakes it errs dangerously, calling a viper a python, which on a trip could cost a life. Plus you get only one free scan, then a 7.99-a-week subscription many mistook for monthly and overpaid.
apps.loved: Everything in one app instead of several, fast work, identifies different objects, saves money on separate apps
apps.weak: Dangerous mistakes on snakes, confuses similar animals and insects, only one free scan, weekly price mistaken for monthly, misses on food and small insects
apps.whoFor: People who want a universal identifier for everyday questions, but not for cases where a mistake is dangerous

quotes.text: I scanned a Russell's Viper which it mistook as an African Rock Python... could be life or death if someone was to use this on a trip like I am on.

apps.title: Plant Identification ++
apps.verdict: There is a core of loyal gardeners who have used it for years and value the detailed plant cards. But most people complain that the app just bounces them to an external website instead of answering, often gets the genus wrong, and asks for extra payment for things promised before purchase. Saving and sharing photos used to work and now doesn't.
apps.loved: Detailed info on plants and trees, help picking plants for the garden, long-standing habit for some gardeners
apps.weak: Redirects to an external site instead of answering, frequent wrong IDs, extra charge for care info, broken photo saving and sharing, no way to cancel
apps.whoFor: Gardeners who want a reference for ornamental plants and are willing to double-check the identification

apps.title: Lens Scan: Identify Anything
apps.verdict: Lens Scan sells identify-anything, and on antiques and collectibles some people find value for estimating worth. But accuracy wobbles: a 19th-century silver mug scanned four times came back as a tureen, a coaster and a hallmark, and a Striker painting as a Banksy print. The core problem is money: clicking the free 3-day trial instantly charges 79-85 dollars, cancelling doesn't help, and it's essentially a paid wrapper over the free Google Lens.
apps.loved: Identifying antiques and collectibles, estimating rough value, saving time on searching
apps.weak: Instant 79-85 dollar charge instead of a free trial, charges after cancellation, inconsistent accuracy on antiques, essentially a paid copy of the free Google Lens
apps.whoFor: Antique dealers and collectors wanting a rough value estimate, if they watch their charges closely

apps.title: Plant Identification－Plantaria
apps.verdict: The app instantly names a plant from a photo of a leaf and appeals to people caring for houseplants, some even grew healthy plants following its advice. But billing torments people at scale: charges during the free trial, keeps charging after cancellation, cancelling is hard, and a third-party processor pulls money outside Apple. It is also not always right, it named only 5 of 23 plants correctly, and often insists on more water when things are fine.
apps.loved: Instant ID from a photo of a leaf, watering reminders, help caring for houseplants, the my garden section
apps.weak: Charges during the trial and after cancellation, hard to cancel, ID mistakes, problem diagnosis does not work, claims of deceptive billing
apps.whoFor: Houseplant lovers willing to fight through billing and tolerate ID misses

quotes.text: The identification process is almost instant. I don't have to wait around for the app to process the image, which is great when I'm on the go.

apps.title: Plantion - Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: The app is meant to name a plant and find its diseases and pests, and it sometimes helps experienced gardeners. But the main feature is broken: for photos of sick leaves and even a dead plant it stubbornly answers healthy, and problem advice boils down to a generic either overwatering or underwatering. ID also drifts, the same plant is named differently under different light, and it gets confused with vegetables.
apps.loved: Identifying plants along with diseases and pests, detailed care information, easy navigation, accuracy with a good photo
apps.weak: Diagnosis answers healthy for everything, even a dead plant, generic advice instead of specifics, ID changes with lighting, confuses vegetables
apps.whoFor: Gardeners fine with a general plant reference, but not for precise disease diagnosis

quotes.text: The app said it will help identify and help my plant may or may not need and every picture says healthy. But I put a picture of a dead plant and it said healthy. A waste of money.

apps.title: Identify My Plant Now
apps.verdict: When it lands, it identifies plants accurately and people love it, one user built a whole landscaping project on it alone. But accuracy drifts: it calls habaneros green peppers, tags citronella as four different plants, and marks half a garden as weeds. The biggest pain is money: 7.99 a week, double and triple PayPal charges, and a promised free that turns into a bill.
apps.loved: Accurate ID on a good shot, care tips, helped with a full landscaping project, tells invasive from native species
apps.weak: Drifting accuracy, calls plants weeds, glitches on photo upload, pricey weekly subscription, double charges
apps.whoFor: Beginner gardeners willing to pay and tolerate the occasional recognition miss

apps.title: Plant Identifier: Plantiary
apps.verdict: Plantiary identifies some plants decently and can log your garden with insect ID too. But accuracy wobbles: it calls a squash a pumpkin and tells you to water aquatic plants that are already underwater. The loudest cry in the reviews isn't about plants, it's about money: the free trial quietly turns into 9.99 a week, cancellation can't be found, and charges continue after cancelling.
apps.loved: Logging a garden with plants and insects, quick on-the-go identification, useful for active gardeners
apps.weak: Confuses similar plants, absurd care advice for aquatic plants, the free trial charges 9.99 a week, no findable cancel button, charges after cancellation
apps.whoFor: Gardeners willing to pay a weekly subscription and watch the cancellation carefully, if they need a garden log with identification

apps.title: AI Plant Identifier・Care－Lily
apps.verdict: The app promises to identify plants and diagnose them with AI, and a couple of people call the tech useful and educational. But the lion's share of reviews are about billing deception: you accept a free trial and money is taken at once, 8.99 turns into 11.99, you get charged twice, there is nowhere to cancel. Real value barely shows in the reviews, many never even got to use it before paying, and the promised two-day diagnosis never arrives.
apps.loved: Educational value about plants, use of AI, helps a family learn about plants
apps.weak: Money taken immediately instead of a free trial, price higher than advertised, double charges, nowhere to cancel, diagnosis not delivered on time, asks for a review before first use
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one without caveats, at best those willing to risk money for plant ID

apps.title: Planto: Plant Identifier
apps.verdict: The app quickly identifies a plant from a photo and can reassure you it is not a weed, which people praise. But disease diagnosis simply will not start for most, no matter how you change the angle, and the feature is capped at a couple of scans a day until you pay. The main trouble is billing: charged every week above what was promised and twice a month, with in-app cancellation blocked by a promise that a team member will reach out within 24 hours, trapping people in endless charges.
apps.loved: Quick ID from a photo, tells you a plant is not a weed, useful care tips, good pictures and descriptions
apps.weak: Disease diagnosis will not start, access limited to a couple of scans a day, weekly and double charges, in-app cancellation blocked, a loop of endless payments
apps.whoFor: Plant lovers who want quick ID, if they cancel right away through Apple settings

quotes.text: I can't get the diagnosis part to work. I have tried every way and angle of picture I can possibly think of and it just won't diagnose.

apps.title: Bug ID - Insect Identifier
apps.verdict: Sometimes it quickly and correctly flags a dangerous spider, which is genuinely reassuring. But the misses are gross: it calls a fly a spider then a fly, cannot handle a bee, reads the same photo differently, and calls a normal photo too small. On top of that sits aggressive monetization: you must subscribe to start, charges run unnoticed for years, and refunds are near impossible.
apps.loved: Fast accurate ID of dangerous spiders in good cases, saving finds in collections, notes on whether bugs are harmful
apps.weak: Gross misses on ordinary insects, answer changes on one photo, calls a normal photo too small, mandatory subscription to start, hidden charges you cannot get back
apps.whoFor: Anxious users wanting a quick check on whether a spider is dangerous, ready for a paywalled entry

quotes.text: I kept resubmitting the same photo and the identification came up different every time.

I needed to quickly identify a red-backed jumping spider that had bitten me. Even though the picture I had wasn't very good, this worked! It was a relief to know that the spider wasn't very dangerous.
I have a perfectly big picture of the bug but it says it's to small. The bug is practically the whole picture and says it's too small.

apps.title: Bug Identifier: AI Insect id
apps.verdict: The app invites you to identify an insect from a photo, and in rare wins a live expert confirms within a couple of days that the bug you found is not a bed bug or a recluse spider, which genuinely reassures. But it identifies poorly and dangerously: it confuses a termite with wasps and bees, a spider with a tick, and the same photo gives different answers. Plus not a single free scan, it demands 30 dollars a year up front for something you will use once or twice, and cancelling is agonizing due to a clunky interface.
apps.loved: A live expert confirms danger within a couple of days, reassures about bed bugs and spiders, quick result in lucky cases
apps.weak: Confuses termites with wasps and spiders with ticks, the same photo gives different answers, not a single free scan, expensive for a couple of uses a year, agonizing cancellation
apps.whoFor: People who rarely get spooked by an unknown insect and want a live expert's opinion, but not at this price

quotes.text: sent in a picture of a spider taken in the US - App misidentified the spider as a variety only found in Europe.

apps.title: Bug Identifier: BugAlert
apps.verdict: The app used to at least point you in a direction, but after switching to AI it answers in vague terms like that is an ant or it is a spider. Real reviews laugh at the misses: it mistook a penny for a bug, gray pants for a monarch, a spider for a bumblebee, and right after scanning an ad pops up that you cannot close. The five-stars about instant alerts are clearly not about this product.
apps.loved: Free to use, sometimes correctly names obvious insects like a bee
apps.weak: Vague speciesless answers after the AI switch, gross misses on household objects, ads right over the result, makes the app pointless to use
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one, only for a very rough bug-versus-butterfly split for free

quotes.text: The ID returned is non-specific butterfly caterpillar worm spider etc. not really what I was looking for.

apps.title: Plant Identifier: ChatPlant AI
apps.verdict: The real reviews are almost unanimous: it gives a different ID for the same photo, fails to recognize an orchid, and answers everything with it is fine, water it. It charges 39 dollars a month for plant treatment while advertising itself as completely free. The glowing five-stars with accuracy percentages stand apart from the picture and look planted.
apps.loved: Quickly identifies the plant species, if identification is all you need
apps.weak: Different answers for the same photo, fails to recognize even an orchid, template advice to just water, expensive subscription disguised as free, lots of ads, hidden cancellation
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one, at most for a rough species ID with no diagnosis and no payment

apps.title: Insect Identifier - Scan Bugs
apps.verdict: The idea is useful but insect recognition is poor: it calls a beetle an ant, a caterpillar a bee, and an invasive spotted lanternfly a common moth. The camera cannot pick up small bugs at all, and the answer can change on the same shot. A free-trial subscription with an unclear exit sours the experience even for people who otherwise like it.
apps.loved: Fast result on a good shot, plenty of reference info on insects, minimal ads per some users
apps.weak: Frequent errors and gross misses, fails on small insects, answer changes on one photo, pushy trial subscription, unclear how to cancel
apps.whoFor: Curious users and students wanting a quick guess, not those needing entomological accuracy

apps.title: Plant Identifier - PlantMe
apps.verdict: PlantMe sells reminders, diagnostics and advice, but by the reviews it rarely lands the identification: it confuses cucumbers with squash, common grass with Bermuda, and one user nearly chopped down his wife's flower on a weed advice. The app forces you to take a live photo and won't let you pick one from your library. On top of that, 8-dollar weekly charges and no way to cancel.
apps.loved: Reminders and diagnostics with advice, easy start for beginners
apps.weak: Frequent wrong IDs even on common vegetables, can't choose a photo from the library, expensive weekly subscription, no way to cancel, forces a 5-star rating on your review
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one except total beginners willing to double-check every result and watch their charges

quotes.text: you cannot use an existing photo. You must take a picture real time for it to work. What if you are in a place without no cell service or can't get back to the area where you took a picture?

apps.title: Smart Identifier: Plant+Insect
apps.verdict: People like the idea that it identifies not just plants but animals too, turning it into a family walk in the woods. In practice accuracy is very low, it calls a flower just a flower, a caterpillar just a caterpillar, confuses Texas ranger with English lavender, and returns nothing on spinach, poppy, or basil. Plus after a couple of snaps it hits you with a paid subscription.
apps.loved: Identifies not just plants but animals too, family nature exploration, wide range of objects
apps.weak: Very low accuracy, answers in vague terms like flower or caterpillar, fails to recognize simple plants, paid subscription after a couple of snaps
apps.whoFor: At most families looking for fun and very rough guessing, not for real identification

quotes.text: I took a picture of a caterpillar to see what kind it was. "Caterpillar" was the answer. Gee thanks.

apps.title: Plant AI: Scanner & Identifier
apps.verdict: People pay and get an endless spinner on the analyze screen that drags on for ten minutes and crashes. When it does answer, it confuses parsley with celery and lemongrass with mint, and fails on a dozen plants in a row. Even the contact-us button is dead, so there is no way to get help.
apps.loved: Almost nothing, the rare positive just says amazing with no detail
apps.weak: Hangs on analysis for ten minutes then crashes, badly confuses plants, no disease diagnosis, broken support contact, paid but delivers nothing
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one, reviewers say ChatGPT is cheaper and more accurate
